analyst.summary: ONGC is India's largest state-run oil and gas producer, trading around 6x earnings with a dividend yield above 5%, but its underlying crude and gas output has been flat to declining for years and keeps missing the company's own production targets -- including its flagship deepwater gas project, whose ramp-up has been pushed out again. Government policy on royalty and gas pricing has swung back and forth even within the last two months, and roughly half of its overseas earnings sit in Russia, adding a geopolitical wrinkle to that portion of the business. The cheap valuation and strong, well-covered dividend make it a reasonable name to hold for income and balance-sheet safety, but there is not yet clear evidence of the production turnaround that would justify treating it as anything more than that.
